[maas-code-reviewer review]

> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


The central idea is sound and correctly implemented: I verified that ServiceCollectionV3 declares every service as a direct class annotation (no annotations inherited from a base class, and src/maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py does not use `from __future__ import annotations`), so create_services_mock() pre-populates the full collection with Mock(service_class), preserving the previous per-test spec semantics (async service methods are auto-detected and become AsyncMock). The mechanical removal of the per-test `services_mock.X = Mock(X)` assignments across all 49 files is consistent, and the type-hint change to `Mock` is appropriate.

Items to address before merge:

1. Dead setup in test_machines.py `endpoints_with_authentication_only` (line 213): the configured `fga_client` is discarded before any request is made, because every base test consuming this fixture calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()`, which rebinds `openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value` to a fresh AsyncOpenFGAClientMock. Notably, the PR description says AsyncOpenFGAClientMock was improved to accept pool permissions, but the diff contains no change to that class — that improvement appears to be missing.

2. Lint: test_machines.py:215 is 83 characters; pyproject.toml sets ruff `line-length = 79` and `make lint` (tox -e lint) runs `ruff format --check` over src/tests/, so CI lint will fail on this line.

3. Systemic behavior shift to be aware of: previously, touching an unassigned service on the specced Mock(ServiceCollectionV3) raised AttributeError (annotation-only names are not in dir(), so the spec rejected them), short-circuiting handlers into a 500 that the base auth tests tolerate. Now handlers run deeper against default MagicMock return values (always truthy, never equal to real ids/usernames), which is why the machines/ipranges/resource_pools authentication-only fixtures needed `get_one`/`get_by_id -> None` patches to keep ownership/pool checks from turning into 403. Future endpoints with object-level checks will likely need the same treatment; consider documenting that contract next to `endpoints_with_authentication_only` in base.py.

4. Minor: create_services_mock iterates raw `__annotations__` (fragile, see inline) and the new comment in base.py mis-explains why the `coroutine was never awaited` warning fires (see inline).

Pre-existing but adjacent: several request-model tests pass a bare MAASResourceEntitlement member to AsyncOpenFGAClientMock although its parameter is typed `set[MAASResourceEntitlement] | None`; this only works because the enum is a StrEnum, so `in` degenerates to a substring test. Worth normalizing while standardizing OpenFGA mock usage.

src/tests/fixtures/__init__.py.71: Raw `ServiceCollectionV3.__annotations__` works today (every service is annotated directly on the class and the module does not use `from __future__ import annotations`), but it is fragile: under PEP 563-style string annotations the values would be strings and `Mock(service_class)` would silently build a string-specced mock, and annotations moved to a base class would be skipped entirely. Both failure modes would resurface as confusing AttributeErrors deep inside handlers. Consider `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceCollectionV3)` (resolves string annotations and merges base-class annotations) or at least assert that each value is a type.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.33: The filter itself is correct and well scoped: CPython emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'x' was never awaited`, which this regex matches. However, the explanation above is inaccurate: the warning fires when a coroutine created by calling a mocked async service method is garbage-collected without ever being awaited — not when 'accessing methods/fields of objects returned by an async method'. Consider rewording so future readers keep the right mental model; also note these filters would hide the same warning if a handler genuinely forgets to await a service call, so keep them limited to these three deliberately-shallow tests.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.213: This `fga_client` setup never takes effect. The only consumer of this fixture, `test_endpoints_require_authentication_only` in base.py, calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()` in the test body, and that factory rebinds `services_mock.openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value` to a fresh `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(set(permissions))` (tests/maasapiserver/fixtures/app.py:199) before any request is made. At request time `list_pools_with_view_machines_access` therefore resolves through `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__` and returns `False`, so `set(view_access_pools)` in `list_machines` (maasapiserver/v3/api/public/handlers/machines.py:120) raises TypeError -> 500, which the `not in (401, 403)` assertion tolerates. The test passes, but not because of these lines. Either drop them, configure the client after the factory call, or extend `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` to accept pool ids — the PR description claims that improvement but the diff does not contain it. Note that the `services_mock.machines.get_one.return_value = None` line below does take effect and is needed for the commission endpoint's 404.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/mo.353: `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__init__` declares `permissions: set[MAASResourceEntitlement] | None`, but a bare enum member is passed here (also at lines 297 and 593). It only works because `MAASResourceEntitlement` is a StrEnum, so `permission in self._permissions` degenerates to a substring test against the member's value — surprising semantics that would break if entitlement values ever overlap as substrings or the enum stops being str-based. Pre-existing, but since this change standardizes OpenFGA mock usage, consider normalizing in `__init__` (accept `MAASResourceEntitlement | set[MAASResourceEntitlement] | None` and wrap single members in a set) so the declared type contract holds.
